senses.gloss: A Christian is a person who believes in salvation from sin through Jesus of Nazareth, called Jesus Christ or Jesus the Christ.
examples: He is a conservative Christian.

senses.gloss: To some religions, a Christian is someone who has a certain spiritual way of being. This is said to be from being spiritually born with the help of Jesus Christ. This is someone who has been saved from sin.
examples: The Baptist preacher said that most Baptists are not really Christians.

senses.gloss: Christian is a male given name.
examples: Hans Christian Andersen is famous for writing books of fairy tales.

senses.gloss: If you are Christian then you are a Christian. (See noun above.)
examples: Yes, she is Christian.

senses.gloss: If something is Christian, it has to do with Christianity.
examples: Being saved from sin by Christ is a Christian idea.
Christmas is a Christian holiday.

senses.gloss: Atheism is the belief that there is no God.
examples: Most atheists say atheism is not a religion.

senses.gloss: Atheism is lacking a belief that God exists.
examples: He explained that his view on god was atheism because there was no evidence of god's existence.

senses.gloss: A mass noun is a noun that refers to an amount, not an item.
examples: "Water" is a mass noun, but "scissors" is not.

senses.gloss: A noun is a kind of word that is usually the name of a person, place, thing, quality, or idea. In English, nouns can be the subject or object of a sentence. They can be singular or plural.
examples: The words "cat", "home", "bread", "Sue" and "sunshine" are nouns.

senses.gloss: Domestic issues relate to issues inside one country, not affecting other countries.

senses.gloss: Domestic issues related to the issues inside one home.
examples: He does his domestic chores.

senses.gloss: A wish, a feeling of want.

senses.gloss: A thing that someone wants.

senses.gloss: To wish for something, to want something.
examples: I desire your company.

senses.gloss: A word used to link two alternative choices.
examples: Would you like tea or coffee?

senses.gloss: Once more.
examples: They didn't understand the answer, so they asked again.

senses.gloss: A knife is a tool that cuts.
examples: He ate with his knife and fork.

senses.gloss: A knife is a tool with a thin edge.
examples: He worked with a putty knife.

senses.gloss: If you knife someone, you stab someone with a knife; you make a hole in them.
examples: The gang knifed him sixteen times.

senses.gloss: AC is a short version of "air conditioning" (cooling).
examples: He turned on the AC to help cool the room.

senses.gloss: AC is also a short version of alternating current.

senses.gloss: A face is the front part of the head.

senses.gloss: A look or expression on the face.

senses.gloss: If x faces y, the front of x is pointing in the direction of y.
examples: Please face me when I speak to you.

senses.gloss: Type, variety.
examples: Bread is a kind of food.

senses.gloss: Good for another person.

senses.gloss: When you feel happy, you feel good, usually because something nice has happened.
examples: He was happy.

senses.gloss: A happy situation or event makes people happy.
examples: It's such a happy day when we can be together again.

senses.gloss: A thing is something.

senses.gloss: The plural form of thing; more than one (kind of) thing.

senses.gloss: An opinion is a personal idea, a person’s thoughts on a topic.

senses.gloss: The beginning of something in place or time.
examples: We went back to the start.

senses.gloss: A movement in reaction to surprise.
examples: I surprised him and he gave a start.

senses.gloss: To begin; to do something for the first time.
examples: They started the race in first place.

senses.gloss: To make a machine begin to work.

examples: The man and the woman kissed each other.

senses.gloss: To touch for a moment.
examples: His car kissed the bumper of the car in front of him.

senses.gloss: A knot is formed when a rope is tied.
examples: He put a knot in the rope.

senses.gloss: A leg is part of a piece of furniture, such as a table, on which the furniture stands.

examples: He was a young man with blue eyes.

senses.gloss: You use man to show your surprise or disappointment.

senses.gloss: If something is manned, it has people to look after it.

senses.gloss: If you man something, you take up position to operate it.
examples: Man the machine guns!

senses.gloss: Man is a surname.
The part of arithmetic where numbers are added together.
examples: He learned addition quickly.
An example of addition is 2+2=4.

senses.gloss: The act of adding something.
examples: The addition of 5 more topics will make the meeting very long and boring.

senses.gloss: You use about to say what subject something is related to.
examples: Let's not talk about her problems.

senses.gloss: If something moves about, it moves in many directions.
examples: He walked about the place, looking everywhere.

senses.gloss: If something is about to happen, it will happen very soon.
examples: Please be seated. We're about to begin.

senses.gloss: To the other side.
examples: I walked across the bridge.

senses.gloss: On the other side.
examples: I can see him across the street.

senses.gloss: If you make something shorter or divide it in pieces, you cut it.

senses.gloss: To hurt with a blade.

senses.gloss: A scratch, opening in the skin or a surface.

senses.gloss: A reduction; lessening.

senses.gloss: A fact is a piece of information.

senses.gloss: An idea is a concept or a thought.

senses.gloss: An idea is something abstract (not concrete).

examples: One boy died and the other is seriously ill in the hospital.

senses.gloss: If you are ill you are angry or disturbed.
examples: You are making me ill with your attacks.

senses.gloss: If you wrong someone, you do something that hurts a person.

senses.gloss: A wrong is an immoral act.

examples: They sail around the world every year in their boat.

senses.gloss: If you sail, you travel on a boat or ship.

senses.gloss: If someone joins someone else, they do something together.

senses.gloss: Enjoyment, fun.
examples: I get a kick out of talking to her.

senses.gloss: If you kick someone or something, you attack or hit it with your foot.

senses.gloss: A quality item is a very good one.

senses.gloss: If you assume something, you think or believe something without having enough information to know that it's true.

examples: The new information showed that his theory about growth was incorrect.
Nobody has disproved Einstein's theory of general relativity.

senses.gloss: A benefit is something good that comes from something else.
examples: It was her idea, but she received no benefit from the new program.

senses.gloss: If you benefit from something, you get something good from it.
examples: My health has really benefited from all the exercise I'm getting.

senses.gloss: Evidence is facts or observations that support an idea.
examples: The gun is evidence that professor Pickle killed Mr. Mustard.

senses.gloss: If a system is online, it is connected (generally electronically) to a larger network.
examples: I do a lot of shopping online, so I almost never have to leave the house.

examples: Since the printer is back online, you should be able to again print from it.

senses.gloss: The present participle of write.

senses.gloss: A subject in school where you write stories and poems.
examples: She is taking a class in creative writing.

senses.gloss: If A is above B, A is higher than or before B, but not touching B.

senses.gloss: An option is a choice.

senses.gloss: If something is ordinary, it is normal and not special.

examples: And he made a cautious approach to the boat.

senses.gloss: Legislation is the official laws and rules of a government.

Three adult males left the bank at 2:14.

something that has been invented

examples: We will explore this idea through an analysis of the public debate on marriage and divorce.
The government's spending programme is the subject of much heated debate.

senses.gloss: If you debate something, you consider its positive and negative points, often by talking with other people in a formal situation such as government.
examples: The AHA had in fact been debating the issue of the future of the hospital for some years.
Few subjects are more hotly debated in curriculum committees.

senses.gloss: A dimension is a part of a problem, issue, or situation.
examples: We need to consider some of the dimensions of the likely future needs for health care among older people.
The baby has added a new dimension to our lives.

senses.gloss: A dimension is a direction of measurement in space time, usually width, depth, and height.
examples: The new viewer lets you examine the image in three dimensions.
The dimensions of the football pitch can actually vary quite considerably with the length being anywhere from 90 m to 120 m.

senses.gloss: If you promote someone or something, you help it to get bigger, higher, or more popular.
examples: The environment provided by the school promotes the reading development of all students.
Remember too that sleepiness is promoted by a warm, quiet environment.

senses.gloss: Output is what is produced by a worker, machine, computer, etc.
examples: We have increased our total output from 4,500 to 7,500 barrels per day of oil.
Of course, any problems with the program will affect the output.

senses.gloss: If you output something, you produce it.
The past tense and past participle of output.
To be alive; to have life.
examples: He's not expected to live for more than a few months.

senses.gloss: To have permanent residence somewhere.
examples: I live at 256 Oak Avenue.

senses.gloss: Having life; something alive.
examples: The post office will not ship live animals.

senses.gloss: A live firearm or explosive is able to cause harm.
examples: The air force practices dropping live bombs on the uninhabited island.

senses.gloss: A live event is an event that happens in real time; direct.
examples: The concert was broadcast live by radio.

senses.gloss: The solution of a mathematical equation.
examples: The result of 1 + 1 is 2.

senses.gloss: The situation at the end of a process, its outcome.
examples: The result of losing the presents was that everyone was sad.
The result of the race was that Peter won.

senses.gloss: If x results in y, it leads to or causes y.
examples: A lot of digging results in a deep hole.

senses.gloss: If x results from y, it comes for or is caused by y.
examples: A deep hole resulted from all the digging.

senses.gloss: A long and narrow piece of land between two places. Usually, cars drive on it, and it is often paved.
examples: The taxi is parked on the side of the road.
The road between the two villages is made of sand.

senses.gloss: The path which one takes to reach a certain place.
examples: It is a long road to the top.
The road from Warsaw to Paris leads through half of Europe.

senses.gloss: If you have access to something, you can use it, look at it, enter it, etc.
examples: As a student, you have access to all our facilities including the library and computers.
We will seek to provide greater access to personal records held by government.

senses.gloss: If you access something, you get information from it, usually using a computer.
examples: The product enables multiple systems to access a single database.
Users of PCs can access images from the photo CDs using any CD-ROM input device.

senses.gloss: Boyfriend normally describes a boy or a young man, who is in a love relationship with another person, when they aren't married yet.
examples: I didn't have a boyfriend, and I thought that it was because I was too fat.

senses.gloss: Boyfriend can also simply mean a friend who is male.
A code is a set of rules or laws.
examples: Children usually learn their parents' moral code.
Section 244(1) (a) of the Canadian Criminal Code defines assault.

senses.gloss: A code is a way of storing or sending information, often secretly or in a way that is readable by computers.
examples: Microsoft has also licensed Windows source code to companies such as Citrix Systems.
In World War II, mathematicians and scientists broke the enemy's secret code.

senses.gloss: If something is coded, it is written or stored in a code.
examples: The completed questionnaires were coded by two people.
The wide variety of proteins in the cells are all coded for by the genes in the nucleus.

senses.gloss: A girlfriend is a girl or young woman who is in a romantic relationship with another person.
examples: Jeremy had been having trouble with his girlfriend.
Koo Stark, a former girlfriend of the Duke of York, was being kept in hospital last night.

senses.gloss: A girlfriend can be any friend who is female.
A phase is stage in a process.
examples: We will look at very basic ideas during the first phase of training.
As the war enters its final phase, the role of the UN will probably become more important.

senses.gloss: If things are in phase, they are working, moving, or changing together.
If you phase something in, you introduce it step by step.
examples: Over the next few years, all farm support was slowly phased out.

senses.gloss: If something happens prior to something else, it happens before it.
examples: In this recipe, most of the work is actually done prior to cooking.
Prior to 1917 most people had lived on private farms.

senses.gloss: occurring before
examples: We learned that police had prior knowledge of the attack.
Few of these workers have any substantial prior experience in industry.

senses.gloss: You use granted to say that you accept that something is true, often before you adding contrasting information.
examples: He's a good student and usually does well. Granted, he did fail that one test, but I think there were good reasons for that.
"You haven't been a very good father." "Granted."

senses.gloss: You use granted that x, y to mean y is true because of x.
examples: Granted that he has done nothing wrong, he should be set free.

senses.gloss: If you take something for granted, you believe it without really knowing or thinking about it.
The past tense and past participle of grant.
Stress is emotional pressure that makes you worry because things are not going well.
examples: Death is a time of great stress for family and friends.
Plants under stress from lack of water or disease are the most likely to attract problem insects.

senses.gloss: Stress is physical pressure that gradually can cause things to break
examples: Sitting puts an unnatural stress on the back and shortens the neck.

senses.gloss: If you stress something, you say that it is very important.
examples: I have repeatedly stressed the importance of hard work, but luck is also helpful.

senses.gloss: If you stress a word, part of a word, or a note in music, you make it louder than other words or notes.
A resolution is a formal decision, often after a vote.
examples: The U.S. may be willing to support a Security Council resolution backing the return of inspectors to Iraq.

senses.gloss: Resolution is the amount of detail that you can see in an image.
examples: This camera is cheaper, but, of course, the resolution is much lower.

senses.gloss: If something is adequate, it is good enough.
examples: It is very hard to provide a simple but adequate explanation.
She left her other job so that she could devote adequate time to the school.

senses.gloss: A tot is a very young or small child.
A total is the final amount of something. It is a term used in math.
If you total something, you add them up.
If something totals something, it adds up to that; it amounts to.
examples: The total of your purchase comes to $53.

senses.gloss: If something is total, it is complete; it is finished.
examples: He is a total failure

senses.gloss: If something is total, it is entire.
examples: The total book was very bad.

senses.gloss: Whole is used to describe every part of an object.
examples: I ate the whole meal, leaving nothing left.

senses.gloss: The whole of something means the entire part of it.
examples: The whole of the Middle East is pretty messy at the moment.

senses.gloss: A half is 1/2 of a whole; 50%.
examples: Sales were down from January to June but jumped in the second half of the year.
Half a year later, the baby was born.

senses.gloss: A half is one part of a game that is divided into two parts.
examples: At the end of the first half, Japan is leading Iran by two points.

senses.gloss: A veterinarian (sometimes shortened to vet) is a doctor that treats animals.
examples: The veterinarian treated the dog.

senses.gloss: If you alter something, you change it, usually in a small way.
examples: The design can be easily altered by selecting new colours, materials, etc.
But not even a good cleaning would alter the fact that the room was dark and unfriendly.

senses.gloss: Stability is the property of being firm and constant.
examples: Investors, especially foreign ones, want political stability to go with economic growth.
He may need handrails on either side for stability and safety.

senses.gloss: Energy is the ability to do work: move, give off heat, give off light, etc.
examples: Unlike coal or oil, atomic energy production creates little air pollution.
Higher electricity prices should help promote energy efficiency.

senses.gloss: If you are aware of something, you know about it.
examples: I am fully aware of the need for security, and will make the necessary changes.
I'm quite aware of the fact that you're here. You don't have to keep reminding me.

senses.gloss: Providence is the careful management of resources.
examples: His providence in saving for his old age is a good example for everyone.

senses.gloss: Providence is God.
A station is a place where many trains or buses stop and people buy tickets and get on.
A station is a place where a person stays in one place and works.
If you station someone, you place them to do a task.

A society is a large number of people and the way they live, talking together, working with each other and making rules and ways to live. A society can be a town, country or more than one country together, with many people living the same ways.
A society is an organization or club that people can join.
To sort is to divide one group of things into smaller groups of things, so that the things in one smaller group are the same as each other in some way.
examples: He sorted the apples, putting red apples in one basket and green apples in the other basket.

senses.gloss: A sort is a kind or type.
examples: Red and green are two sorts of apple.

senses.gloss: A small person or thing is not big. It doesn't have much size.
examples: A mouse is a small animal. A baby mouse is very small.

senses.gloss: Something is slow if it takes a long time to move. It is not fast.
examples: A snail is a very slow animal. It moves slowly.

senses.gloss: If something is slow, it does not happen in a short time.
If you slow someone or something, he, she, or it does not move as quickly as he, she, or it did before; you lower the speed of something.
If you slow, you do not progress as quickly as you did before.
A slope is one side of a hill.
examples: We will have to climb up this slope to get to the top of the hill.

senses.gloss: The slope of a line is how far up it goes divided by how far along it goes.
If something slopes, it goes either up or down.
examples: The hill slopes down at this point.

senses.gloss: A long thing is slanting when one end is higher up than the other end and also further along. To be on an angle or sloping.
examples: The piece of wood is slanting from the ground up to the door so that a cart with wheels can roll up it.

senses.gloss: A slant is the way a long thing is when one end is higher up and further along than the other end. The way a ramp is.
Enforcement is the act of making people follow a law, rule, or decision.
examples: It is not a problem which can be solved by law enforcement alone.
There simply hasn't been enough enforcement of the rules during this tournament.

senses.gloss: When something slides, or moves a small distance while touching what it's on, we say it slips.
examples: The hat slipped down until it covered her eyes.

senses.gloss: When someone or something moves without wanting to move, we say it slips.
examples: My foot slipped when I stepped on some ice, and I almost fell.

senses.gloss: A slip is a small mistake.
A slip is a piece of clothing like a small white skirt, that a woman sometimes wears hidden under her skirt or dress.
A draft is a piece of writing which has been or may be edited.
examples: In the first draft of the story the characters names are all different.
Check final drafts for misspellings, using a dictionary or computer spelling checker.

senses.gloss: A draft is when the military or a sport team chooses its members.
examples: Many Americans moved to Canada to avoid the draft during the war.
The Tigers' first choice in yesterday's draft was pitcher George Berlin.

senses.gloss: If you draft a letter, memo, agreement, etc., you write one that has been or may be edited.
examples: You should have the contract drafted by a lawyer.

senses.gloss: If a state drafts someone, it chooses them to be in the military.
examples: I was drafted when I was 20 and spent two years fighting in France.

senses.gloss: If something is precise it is correct and exact.
examples: Young children are often unable to give a precise definition for words they know very well.
The precise nature of the tax changes has not been decided.

senses.gloss: If someone is precise they always act and speak very carefully.
The sky is what you see when you look up when you're not inside. It's blue with clouds in it. At night it's black with stars in it.
examples: The night sky was full of stars.

senses.gloss: If you pursue a job or hobby, you do it for a long time.
examples: The band motivated her to pursue a career in music.

senses.gloss: If you pursue someone or something, you try to reach, catch or get it.
If something is symbolic, it has or is used as a symbol.
examples: In many religions, the number 3 has a symbolic value.
The apology was purely symbolic and did nothing to change the situation.

senses.gloss: If something is marginal, it is not very large, important or central.
examples: But this discussion is marginal to the real issue.

senses.gloss: (in finance) The marginal profit, tax rate, etc. is the percent earned or paid on one more unit of production or income.
examples: Large scale economies tend to mean that the marginal cost of serving an additional customer is either zero or very small.

senses.gloss: A strong soft material that cloth is made of. A certain type of silk worms make it.
examples: This shirt is made of silk.

senses.gloss: A flat thing with a few words or pictures on it to tell people something.
examples: I saw a stop sign, so I stopped the car.

senses.gloss: When someone signs a piece of paper, they write their signature on it.
examples: They signed a contract saying exactly who would do the work and how much money they would be paid.

senses.gloss: If a company signs someone, they hire them to work.
A side is a straight edge of an object.
examples: A square has four sides.

senses.gloss: A side is the left part or the right part of something.
examples: This car has only one door on each side.

senses.gloss: (usually with "with") To side with someone is to be in an alliance with them.
examples: Who will you side with, Bob or Rachel?

senses.gloss: The capacity of a container, room, etc. is how much it can hold.
examples: The capacity of the bottle is 500 ml.
The capacity of the hard drive is 120 GB.

senses.gloss: The capacity of someone or something to do something is the ability to do it.
examples: I was impressed by his energy and capacity for hard work.
Since the head injury he has lost his capacity to learn new names.

senses.gloss: If x has exposure to y, x is not hidden or protected from y.
examples: Staying out of the sun between 11am and 3pm can reduce exposure by 60 per cent.
Prolonged exposure to cold and wet may increase the chance of disease.

senses.gloss: The exposure is the amount of time that a film is hit by light.
If you modify something, you change it, often only in small ways, and often because you want to use it in a different situation.
examples: Both penalties and rewards can be used to modify children's behaviour.
It is also possible to modify the original by adding or removing parts.

senses.gloss: If a word, phrase, or clause modifies another, it is an optional word, phrase, or clause that gives more information about the other.
examples: The adjective "big" modifies the noun "bridge" in the expression "big bridge".

senses.gloss: Something that is external is not on the inside.
examples: Both internal and external stairs need to be modified to allow wheelchairs into the building.
There are many influences upon the child external to life in school.

senses.gloss: If something is fundamental, it is basic and important.
examples: The loss of her legs has caused her to undergo a fundamental change in how she looks at life.
Respect is fundamental to a strong education system.

senses.gloss: The fundamentals of something, are the main ideas or parts that it is built on.
A flash is a sudden bright light.
examples: He used the flash on his camera.

senses.gloss: A flash is a very fast period of time.
examples: The tall man disappeared in a flash.

senses.gloss: If something flashes, it shines brightly and suddenly.
examples: The fountain flashed in the sunshine.
It rained hard. Lightning flashed and we heard thunder.

senses.gloss:
:
 This short section needs someone to add to it.
A ratio is the comparison in size or number between two things. It is written x:y and read x to y. It is the same as the fraction x/y.
examples: The ratio of men's jobs to women's is 8 to 1.
But Germany now has one of the highest ratios of spending to GDP in the European Community.

senses.gloss: When someone moves a door so that people can't go through it, the person is shutting the door. When someone puts their lips together so that no air or food can go in or out of their mouth, the person is shutting their mouth.
examples: The wind was too cold, so I shut the window.

senses.gloss: Two shoes are two things that someone wears on their feet. Shoes have a hard, flat bottom.
If you shoe, you put shoes on your feet. We usually use this verb as a past participle: We say say someone is shod if they have shoes on their feet.
examples: He was dressed and shod, ready to go out.

senses.gloss: If you shoe a horse, you put horseshoes on the horse.
A shock is the way it feels when a heavy thing suddenly hits another thing.
A shock is a sudden change that surprises people.
Someone is shocked when they are surprised at something
examples: He was shocked at how much she had changed since he had last met her.

senses.gloss: If someone has been shocked, they got a painful feeling due to electricity flowing through their body.
A shelf is a flat thing that people can put books or other things on when they are not using them.
Someone feels shame when they know they did something wrong.
examples: The boy felt shame and gave back the candy he had taken.

senses.gloss: If you shame someone, you make them feel shame.
To shake is to move from side to side many times quickly.
examples: She shook the bottle to mix the drink.

senses.gloss: A shake is a type of beverage.
examples: They were known for their shakes.

senses.gloss: A shake is when something shakes.
A shade is a shadow of a tree or another big thing that blocks some of the light and heat of the Sun.
examples: She rested in the shade of the tree because she felt hot.

senses.gloss: A shade is the slight difference between colors.
If something is shaded, it is shielded from light.
examples: The old tree shaded the animals from the sun.

senses.gloss: If something is shading, it is approaching something slightly.
examples: The grassland was green, shading towards brown in the drier areas.

senses.gloss: When we say one thing versus another thing, it means the two things are on different sides, going in different directions, or against each other.
examples: Tonight's game has Toronto versus Montreal.
A lot of people see America as poor versus rich versus a middle class.

senses.gloss: A terminal is the end of a train track or bus route. It is the station or the last stop.
examples: The bus drove into the terminal and all the people got off.

senses.gloss: A computer screen and keyboard, which are at the end of a wire joining them to a computer.
examples: She sat at the computer terminal and typed some words.

senses.gloss: The last. At the end, in time or in space. A terminal illness is a sickness that will make the person die.
The takeoff is when an airplane moves from the ground into the air.
examples: Put on your seat belt to be ready for takeoff.

senses.gloss: When an army stops fighting and lets the other side win, we say that the army surrenders. Sometimes people wave a white flag to show that they are surrendering.
To submit to a person who has more power.
A surrender is the act of surrendering.
You use whereas to show a contrast between two things or ideas.
examples: Many kinds of roses have little or no scent, whereas others are well known for their beautiful smell.
School A has about 25 percent Asian students, whereas for school B the Asian students make up over 60 percent of the school population.

senses.gloss: Because.
If you enable something or someone, you make make it able to do something or you help it.
examples: The program enables users to share data, collaborate and automate tasks without writing any extra code.
Night or instrument flying enabled us to fly twenty-four hours a day and in poor weather.

senses.gloss: A version is something that exists in different forms.
examples: Tomorrow, IBM is launching OS/2 2.0, the new version of its OS/2 operating software for personal computers.
The North American version of the car will have a larger engine.

senses.gloss: A perspective is a way of looking at or thinking about something.
examples: The British media give a completely different perspective from CNN.
He has to look at everything from an international perspective.

senses.gloss: Perspective is the ability to think about things in a reasonable way.
examples: He's lost all perspective when it comes to this job.

senses.gloss: A network is a group of connections between a number of points.
examples: Electronic systems control the busiest parts of the rail network.
This is the first national TV network that is 100% sports.

senses.gloss: If you network, you make or use social connections, usually for business purposes.
examples: I spent most of my time at the conferences networking with other sales people.

senses.gloss: Someone's welfare is their health, safety, and other things the make them happy.
examples: Children need to exercise each day, for both their physical and psychological welfare.
This group has tried to promote the welfare of old people throughout the United Kingdom.

senses.gloss: Welfare is money paid by the government to poor people.
examples: The government is reviewing the welfare benefits which single parents receive.
He lost his job and his home and has had to go on welfare.

senses.gloss: A transition is a change from one place or situation to another.
examples: Diana has made the transition from girl to woman.
The transition from ice to water occurs at 0°C.

senses.gloss: If something transitions, it changes from one place or situation to another.
An amendment is an addition or change to a document; also the process of making this change.
examples: This law can only be changed by constitutional amendment.
We are considering an amendment to the Water Bill which required compliance with EC rules by 1993.

senses.gloss: A hole or body of water is deep if it goes down a long way.
examples: Do not dive into this swimming pool because it is not deep enough.
Some oil wells must be drilled deeper than others to reach the oil.

senses.gloss: Something is deep if it is far below or inside.
examples: The Earth's iron core is deep beneath its crust.
The Japanese style of poetry called haiku is simple on the surface, but it should also have a deeper emotional meaning.

senses.gloss: If you reject an idea or belief, you decide that you do not believe it.
examples: We reject the idea that English is somehow "better" than other languages.
The court rejected his arguments that he should be set free.

senses.gloss: If you reject a person, you refuse to care for that person.
examples: Often people who are infected with AIDS are rejected by family and friends.

senses.gloss: A reject is something that has been rejected.
A reject is a stupid person.
A clause is a section in a contract or other legal document.
examples: The author's contract contained a clause giving him creative control over the films.

senses.gloss: A clause is a group of words that usually includes a subject and a predicate. In English, the subject usually comes before the predicate.
examples: The last clause in the sentence is hard to understand without knowing some background.

senses.gloss: A predicate is the head of a clause and says something about the subject.
If you predicate something, you state or assert it.
If you predicate that something is true, you state that it is true.
examples: The article predicates that the market collapse was caused by weakness of the dollar.

senses.gloss: If something is prime, it is best, most important, most suitable, or in some way number one.
examples: Canada is a prime example of a multicultural country.
He was the prime suspect in the murder investigation.

senses.gloss: The prime is the best part of something.
examples: He was killed at the prime of his life.

senses.gloss: A prime is a number that can be evenly divided only by one and itself.
examples: The first six primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, and 13.

senses.gloss: If you prime something, you get it ready to do something.
examples: The coach has primed them for the game.

senses.gloss: to manipulate, in a subtle manner, people's decision-making by use of symbols, location, etc.
An objective is something that you are trying to do.
examples: The main objective of our visit was to climb Mount Kenya.
I share the objective of everyone in Britain who want our soldiers home.

senses.gloss: An objective is a place you want to get to.
If something is objective, it is based on facts and things we can see and touch without using people's feelings.
examples: It is hard to find objective measures of artistic ability.
Newspapers try hard to publish objective stories.

senses.gloss: If someone is objective, they are thinking about things logically based on facts.
examples: Watching the play on TV can help an actor to be more objective about his performance.

senses.gloss: If two things are equivalent, they are of equal value or acceptability.
examples: Dolphins have very large brains, roughly equivalent to the size of a human brain.

senses.gloss: An equivalent is something of equal value of acceptability.
examples: Living in Thailand costs the equivalent of just £10 per day.

senses.gloss: If something is liberal, it allows for change, flexibility, and free thought.
examples: The Church should take a more liberal view of sex.
Japanese schools are quite different from what you see in our more liberal education system.

senses.gloss: If something is liberal, it has few limits.
examples: He was quite liberal with his kindness.

senses.gloss: A liberal is a person who believes in liberal ideas.
A notion is an idea about something.
examples: The film questions the standard notions of right and wrong.
We have to reject this strange notion that some languages are better than others.

senses.gloss: A substitution is the act of replacing one person or thing with another.
examples: The accidental substitution of one medicine for another can be deadly.
They had no extra players, so were unable to make any substitutions.

senses.gloss: If you generate something, you create it.
examples: On the hottest summer days, we are unable to generate enough electricity.
Apple is great at generating interest in their computers and other products.

senses.gloss: Revenue is the money that a business receives for doing business, and government receives from taxes.
examples: Higher oil prices should raise government revenue by 13%.
Individual taxpayers today provide a bigger share of our tax revenues than they did before.

senses.gloss: A compound is a material made of a number of other materials.
examples: The new chemical compound has far less smell than the original substance.
There is a group of gases that do not easily form chemical compounds.

senses.gloss: A compound is a mixture.
examples: The new CD is a compound of North American rock music and Middle Eastern religious songs.

senses.gloss: If something is compounded, it is added to.
examples: Her troubles were now compounded by the rain.

senses.gloss: If interest is compounded, it is paid on earlier interest payments.
examples: Interest is compounded monthly.

senses.gloss: Evolution is the process of slow change. It is most used in biology to refer to the way living things change over long periods of time in order to adapt to their surroundings.
examples: The theory of evolution is the basis of modern biology.
For the first time, the evolution of some bacteria has been observed.

senses.gloss: An evolution is a change that happens over time.
examples: Over the last ten years, there has been an evolution in the way we think about this disease.

senses.gloss: ordinal eighteenth) Eighteen is the number that is after seventeen and before nineteen. It can also be written as 18.
examples: Eighteen chickens sat on the roof.

senses.gloss: The number 18.
examples: Two nines is eighteen.

senses.gloss: A set of eighteen things or persons.
examples: The eighteen were leaving the city.

senses.gloss: ordinal eleventh) Eleven is the number that is after ten and before twelve. It can also be written as 11.
examples: Eleven trees stood on the hill.

senses.gloss: The number 11.
examples: Eleven is a prime number.

senses.gloss: A set of eleven things or persons.
examples: Ocean's eleven are a group of thieves.
The girl looked young, no older than eleven.

senses.gloss: ordinal fifteenth) Fifteen is the number that is after fourteen and before sixteen. It can also be written as 15.
examples: Fifteen ducks swim on the lake.

senses.gloss: The number 15.
examples: Five and ten makes fifteen.

senses.gloss: A set of fifteen things or persons.
examples: The fifteen were leaving the city.

senses.gloss: ordinal ninety-ninth) Ninety-nine (99) is the odd number that comes before one hundred.
examples: Ninety-nine apples lay on the table.

senses.gloss: ordinal ninetieth) Ninety is an even number. In numerals, it is 90.
examples: Ninety years ago, things were different.

senses.gloss: The number 90.
examples: Ninety is ten less than hundred and forty more than fifty.

senses.gloss: To be 90 years old.
examples: My grandfather is ninety.

senses.gloss: ordinal nineteenth) Nineteen is the number that is after eighteen and before twenty. It can also be written as 19.
examples: Nineteen ducks swim on the lake.

senses.gloss: The number 19.
examples: Nine and ten makes nineteen.

senses.gloss: A set of nineteen things or persons.
examples: The nineteen are the fastest runners in their school.

senses.gloss: ordinal twelfth) Twelve is the number that is after eleven and before thirteen. In numerals, it is 12.
examples: Twelve eggs make a big omelette.

senses.gloss: The number 12.

senses.gloss: Paste is a thick liquid for sticking (attaching) things together. Paste is like glue, but glue is more liquid and paste is more solid.
examples: He mixed flour and water to make a paste for sticking the paper together.

senses.gloss: Any very thick liquid, almost solid.
examples: Tomato paste is good in sauce to put on rice or spaghetti.

senses.gloss: If you paste something in a computer program, you cut or copy it from one place and put a copy of it somewhere else.
To stick things together using paste.
examples: She pasted the pictures onto the wall.

senses.gloss: A package; a box wrapped in paper; a thing bigger than a letter that is sent in the mail.
examples: On my birthday, I got a parcel in the mail.

senses.gloss: A parcel of land is a piece of land that was part of a larger piece.
If you parcel something out, you divide it into small parts to give to different people.
examples: The set of books was parcelled out among the people who were there.

senses.gloss: If you parcel something off, you divide it into small parts to be sold to different people.
The owner of a thing is the person who owns the thing: who has the thing or who should have the thing. A thing belongs to its owner.
examples: Who is the owner of this coat that was left on a chair?
You have to give it back to me. I'm the owner.

senses.gloss: An oven is for cooking food. It's hot and people put food inside it.
examples: Leave the cake in the oven for thirty minutes.

senses.gloss: An ornament is something that is put onto something or someone just to look beautiful and for no other reason.
examples: One ring on her finger was the only ornament she wore.
We put ornaments on the Christmas tree.

senses.gloss: If you ornament something, you decorate or add to it.
examples: Let's ornament the tree with lights to make it more festive.

senses.gloss: Order is when things are where they should be.
examples: I need to take some time to put my things in order.

senses.gloss: The order of some things means which thing is first, which one is second, which one is last, etc.
examples: The children will take turns in order of age.

senses.gloss: To order something is to ask someone to sell it to you.
examples: At the restaurant, she ordered chicken and potatoes.

senses.gloss: To order someone to do something is to tell the person that they must do it.
examples: The father ordered his children to be quiet.

senses.gloss: The other people or things, are those apart from the ones we have or were talking about.
examples: No, don't put it on this table. Put it on the other table.
The people inside are OK, but the other people are getting wet.

senses.gloss: more
examples: There are many other kinds of problems.
Do you have any other questions?

senses.gloss: Others are those apart from the ones we have or were talking about.
examples: Thanks for the books. I'll get the others tomorrow.
Wow, this is a lot. How many others are there?

senses.gloss: Other is a male given name.
Other is a surname.
no more than; no other than; just
examples: There are only three schools in this town.
You can get this only in Canada.

senses.gloss: Just one or just a few; this and no other; no more than this.
examples: She is the only woman doctor in this city.
These are the only coins I have.

senses.gloss: An only child, son, girl, etc. has no brothers or sisters.
You use only to introduce a fact that prevents a statement from being completely true.
examples: They probably could do it, only you never let them try.

senses.gloss: Observation is the act of carefully seeing things that happen.
examples: To learn, you must be good at observation.

senses.gloss: An observation is something someone saw, heard etc.
examples: In science, we record our observations so we can think about them later.

senses.gloss: A note is a single sound in music.
examples: In this song, every word is on a different note.

senses.gloss: A note is a short letter; something written on a small piece of paper.
examples: If you go out, leave me a note to tell me where you went.

senses.gloss: You note that something happened when you see that it happened and remember it.
examples: I noted that you weren't wearing shoes.

senses.gloss: North is the direction towards the top of the Earth, opposite to south; If you are looking north, the sun sets on your left.
examples: Canada is the biggest country in North America.

senses.gloss: North is the end of a magnet that points north.
In the direction north; towards the north
examples: The place you want is two miles north of here.
It's colder here because we're further north.

senses.gloss: North is a surname.
News is information about things that happened a short time ago, especially on the radio, TV or in newspapers.
examples: Did you hear the news that the war just ended?
Do you have any news about Paul's sickness?

senses.gloss: A net is a thing made of ropes or string that lets small things through but keeps big things in.
examples: I forgot my fishing net. What will we use to catch fish now?
The tennis player hit the ball into the net.

senses.gloss: To net something is to catch it in a net.
examples: He netted a big fish.

senses.gloss: A company's net income is its profits minus its expenses.
A nerve is a cell in the body that sends signals. The brain is made of nerves.
examples: She can't feel anything with this arm, and can't move her arm, because the nerves were cut in an accident.

senses.gloss: Nerve is confidence: a feeling of being able to do something.
examples: He didn't have the nerve to ask her to dance.
You had a lot of nerve, saying that to me! Go away!

senses.gloss: A needle is a small, long, thin sharp metal thing with a hole in it, used for sewing.
examples: She used a needle and blue thread to fix the hole in the shirt.

senses.gloss: A needle is a long, thing, sharp metal thing for putting drugs into a person through the skin.
examples: The doctor used the needle to inject the medicine into the patient.

senses.gloss: To tease; to make fun of.
examples: Billy needled his sister incessantly about her pimples.

senses.gloss: A compliment is a few words of praise: saying that someone or something is good in some way.
examples: William gave me a compliment and that made me feel good. He told me my hair was nice.

senses.gloss: Compliment means to praise someone.
examples: She complimented him on his clothes because they looked good.

senses.gloss: A conjunction is a word used to join words, phrases, clauses, or sentences.
examples: The word or is a conjunction because it can join two words: Tell me if you see a red or blue car.
The word that can be used as a conjunction: I think that you are right.

senses.gloss: Three common conjunctions
A conviction is when a court finds a person guilty of doing a crime.
examples: There was a conviction in his case, so he went to jail.

senses.gloss: A conviction is a strong belief that you think is true.
examples: Because of their strong conviction, I begin to feel that they may be right.

senses.gloss: A place or person is peaceful when there is silence or quiet. There is no noise and nothing happening suddenly.
If you need something, you want it and must have it.
examples: Everyone needs food and water.

senses.gloss: If you need to do something, it is very important for you to do it.
examples: Sir, you need to leave now.

senses.gloss: If you need do something, you have to do it.
examples: Need you do that all the time?
You needn't keep telling me. I heard you the first time.

senses.gloss: If you have a need for something, you must have it; something necessary or required.
examples: I've always tried to have few needs beyond food, clothing and shelter.

senses.gloss: Something is necessary if people need it. It must happen or there will be a big problem.
examples: It's necessary to stop when you see a red light.

senses.gloss: A necessary is a bathroom.
Something is natural if people didn't make it.
examples: Animals, plants and rocks are natural things.

senses.gloss: Something is natural if it's the way it usually is, without people changing it, or is a way that is not a surprise.
examples: It's only natural for you to think that.

senses.gloss: A nail is a small, long, thin sharp metal thing for holding wood together. People put it into the wood by hitting it with a hammer.
examples: I need some nails to fix the roof.

senses.gloss: A nail is the thick, hard part at the ends of fingers and toes.
examples: I broke the top off my finger nail and it was very painful.

senses.gloss: If you nail something to something else, you use a nail to join them.
examples: He nailed the set of shelves onto the wall.

senses.gloss: When someone gets an idea just right, we say they nailed it or "hit the nail on the head".
examples: I think you've nailed the reason why this isn't working.

senses.gloss: A muscle is a part of the body of a person or animal. It's a part that pulls to make parts of the body move.
examples: He can lift heavy things because he has strong muscles.

senses.gloss: To muscle is to use strength or muscles to do something.
examples: He muscled his way into the room between the people who were trying to stop him.

senses.gloss: The moon is the shining white and grey object in the sky at night. It appears to change shape from round (a full moon) to a crescent and back again. It's like a small planet that goes around the Earth.
examples: I was able to see the road because there was a full moon that night.

senses.gloss: A moon is a thing like a small planet that goes around another planet.
examples: Galileo saw four moons of Jupiter: Callisto, Europa, Ganymede and Io.

senses.gloss: If you moon someone, you show them your bare buttocks.
examples: Someone in the car pulled down their pants and mooned us as they drove past.

senses.gloss: A monkey is a primate with a long tail that climbs trees.
examples: We saw Vervet monkeys in the Zoo.

senses.gloss: If you monkey something, you make changes to it.
examples: I foolishly monkeyed with the control panel and it ended up exploding.

senses.gloss: A minute is a short time equal to sixty seconds. There are sixty minutes in one hour.
examples: He ran the race in 1 minute and ten seconds.

senses.gloss: A minute is a short time.
examples: Please wait a minute while I get my coat and then I will come with you.

senses.gloss: Minute things are small.
examples: The pictures appear similar, with only a few, minute differences.

senses.gloss: Someone's mind is the part of them that thinks.
examples: In my mind I know I must go, but in my heart I want to stay here.
We will solve this problem. We have the best minds in the country working on it.

senses.gloss: If you mind some action or thing, you feel negatively about it.
examples: "Do you mind if I sit here?" "No, not at all"
"It's raining outside. You should take an umbrella" "It's OK, I don't mind the rain"

senses.gloss: If you mind someone or something, you look after it.
examples: "Could you mind the children while I go to the bathroom?"

senses.gloss: If something is military, it is a characteristic of people in the armed forces.
examples: Sick soldiers go to the military hospital.

senses.gloss: If something is military, it is about armed forces such as the army, marines, navy, or air force.
A military is armed forces.
The military is the United States armed forces in general.
examples: It's not the job of the military to make policy.

senses.gloss: The place that is between two things; the place that is halfway between two ends of something.
examples: Cut the wood exactly in the middle to get two pieces of equal size.
The middle of the three books is the one you want.

senses.gloss: When someone remembers something, we call the thing they remember a memory.
examples: I have very nice memories of the time when my children were young.

senses.gloss: The part of the mind that remembers; the act of remembering.
examples: When we get older, our memory isn't as good.

senses.gloss: A meeting is when a group of people come together to talk about something important.
examples: The meeting will be in the green room after lunch. I hope you'll be there.

senses.gloss: The present participle of meet.

A man and a woman are married if they are husband and wife to each other. Usually when two people are married they live in the same house and they often have children. Two people have a special day to become married.
examples: I don't need to meet more young men—I'm already married.

senses.gloss: If two things are married they have been made into one thing.
examples: Music and television are married in music videos.

senses.gloss: The past and past participle of marry.
A mark is a single line left by a pen or pencil, or any small bit of color that got onto something.
examples: You have a mark on your shirt from that tomato sauce you were eating.

senses.gloss: If you mark something, you put a mark on it.
examples: The big rock marked the side of the car a little when she drove too close to it.
I marked the boxes so we would know which ones are mine.

senses.gloss: If you mark something, you notice it or pay attention to it.
examples: Mark my words!

senses.gloss: Mark is a male given name.
When someone loves another person, they feel good about the person and want the person to be happy.
examples: I love Colin.
Mothers love their children very deeply.

senses.gloss: The feeling of loving someone and caring for them.
examples: Is my love for him a real love that will last a long time?

senses.gloss: To love someone or something means to like someone or something very much.
examples: I love the simple English Wikipedia.

senses.gloss: A loss happens when something goes where people can't find it. People don't know where the thing is or they don't have it any more.
examples: The loss of my keys means I can't go into my house today.

senses.gloss: Loss is when someone's loved one dies. When someone dies, they are no longer with you.
examples: I loss both of my grandparents from old age.

senses.gloss: Someone looks at something when they move their head or move their eyes so that they can see the thing.
examples: Look at this picture! Isn't it beautiful?

senses.gloss: The way that something looks is the way that it appears.
examples: A new car looks very nice until it gets dirty.
That doughnut looks delicious.

senses.gloss: A lock is a metal thing on a door (or on a window, drawer, etc.) that stops people from opening the door unless they have the right key to open it.
examples: No one will take things from my house. I have a very strong lock on the door.

senses.gloss: A lock is two or more gates (doors) in water to let boats move from lower water to higher water or the other way.
Someone locks a door when they close the lock with a key so that no one can come in.
examples: Remember to lock the door when you leave the house.

senses.gloss: The present participle of live.
A way of earning money.
examples: What do you do for a living?

senses.gloss: A living thing is a person, animal or plant that is not dead—it is still able to function and grow.
examples: Living things grow and make more living things like themselves.

senses.gloss: Linen is a material that some cloth is made of. It comes from the flax plant, and in the past, bed sheets were often made from it, before cotton was used.
examples: This shirt is made of linen.

senses.gloss: Linens are something made from linen, especially bed sheets.
examples: Would you like to change the linens on your bed?

senses.gloss: A line is a mark that is long, straight and very thin.
examples: She drew a line down the middle of the page to divide the page into two parts.

senses.gloss: A line is a row.
examples: Put the buttons in a straight line on the front of the shirt.

senses.gloss: Someone lines things up when they put them in a straight line or row.
Someone lines something up when they put it just in the right place or at the edge of something.
examples: Line up the end of the piece of wood with the edge of the table.

senses.gloss: Someone lifts something when they use their hands to make the thing go up.
examples: He lifted the little boy onto his shoulders.
She lifted the heavy box from the floor onto the table.

senses.gloss: If you give someone a lift, you drive them somewhere, usually in your car.
A lift is a machine that lifts people up or down to different parts of a building.
Even, flat, straight, smooth, horizontal. Having all parts equally as high as all other parts.
examples: This table is not level: things are rolling off it.

senses.gloss: If one thing is level with another, they are at the same height.
examples: The bookshelf is level with the top of the door frame.

senses.gloss: A level is a place that is higher or lower than some other places.
examples: The room you want is on the third level of this building.

senses.gloss: A tool for finding out whether a surface is level.

Someone laughs when they make a sound with their mouth because they think something is funny. It can sound like "ha ha", "ho ho", "hee hee", etc.
examples: That was a really good joke. I've never laughed so hard!

senses.gloss: The sound of someone laughing, or the action of laughing.
examples: We had lots of good laughs at the party.
I heard a laugh in the other room and went to see what they were laughing at.

senses.gloss: Happening or coming after all other similar things or people.
examples: I was the last person to go there: when I went, the others were all already there.
My house is the last house at the end of the street.

senses.gloss: To endure, continue over time.
examples: Summer seems to last longer each year.

senses.gloss: To hold out, continue undefeated or entire.
examples: I don't know how much longer we can last without reinforcements.

senses.gloss: Last week, month, year, etc. is the one that comes before this one.
examples: I didn't see you last week.
I haven't seen him since the summer before last.

senses.gloss: An interest is when a person wants to know more about someone or something or likes someone or something or likes to do something.
examples: She has a strong interest in art. She is going to go to an art school.
What are your interests?

senses.gloss: An interest is when someone or something is important to a person, or if good things happening to the thing are good for the person.
examples: Because I own a house on this street, I have an interest in keeping the street clean.
I'm doing this to look after my own interests.

senses.gloss: If a person is interested, they are curious and want to find out about someone or something.
examples: I am interested in researching flowers.
Does maths interest you?

senses.gloss: The limit is the edge of how far something can go. It can go up to the limit but no farther.
examples: This fence is at the limit of my property.
The heater sets a limit to how cold it can be in the house; it can't get colder than that.

senses.gloss: To make something stay inside a limit.
examples: The fence limits the cows from going out of the field.

senses.gloss: If you limit someone, you reduce or take away their freedom.
ordinal twentieth) The number 20.
examples: I was in university when I was twenty years old.

senses.gloss: A twenty is a 20 dollar bill.
examples: I'd like my $50 as 1 twenty, 2 tens and 2 fives.

senses.gloss: "Twenty" is short for 10-20, meaning location.
examples: Jason, what's your twenty?

senses.gloss: ordinal thirtieth) The number 30.
examples: I had my first child when I was thirty years old.

senses.gloss: The number 30.
examples: Three tens is thirty.

senses.gloss: The scope of a book, a law, a duty, etc. is how much is included or how far it can go.
examples: The small budget has limited the scope of the research.
There are plans to expand the scope of the department's activities.

senses.gloss: A scope is an instrument for looking at things, e.g., a telescope or a microscope.
If you scope something (out), you look at it carefully.
examples: I scoped out the place last week. It seems nice.

senses.gloss: If you enhance something, you make it bigger or better.
examples: He can greatly enhance his reputation by winning tonight.
Our aim is to enhance the quality of life for the British people.

senses.gloss: If you have control over someone or something, you can make it do what you want.
examples: He should try to take control and tell the other handlers what to do.
Driving in the rain, he had lost control on the wet surface and spun off the road.

senses.gloss: A control is a button, switch, dial, etc. that lets you make a machine do what you want.
examples: If you turn off your TV with the remote control, it continues to use a quarter of normal power.
She touched the volume control and the sound dropped.

senses.gloss: If you control something, you make it do what you want.
examples: Too many people are overweight because they can't control their eating behaviour.
The company is controlled by a New York businessman.

senses.gloss: If you control something, you do not let its numbers or size grow too much.
examples: The new plan should control inflation.

senses.gloss: If something is high, it is a long way up.
examples: The airplane flew very high.

senses.gloss: If something is high, its top is a long way up.
examples: That is the highest mountain near here.

senses.gloss: A lead is a wire or strap attached to something.
examples: The dog can't go far because it's on a short lead.
Attach this lead to one end of the battery.

senses.gloss: Lead is a very heavy gray metal. It's a chemical symbol is Pb.
examples: This box is so heavy, it feels as if it's full of lead.

senses.gloss: Someone is leading other people if the person is going first and the other people are following or coming after.
examples: Please lead us to the house, because you know how to go there.

senses.gloss: Showing or telling other people what to do.
examples: He moves that little stick in the air to lead the people making music.

senses.gloss: A written record of a saying or action of the Prophet Muhammad. Used as a basis for conduct in Islamic practices.
Insurance is an agreement where someone pays a small amount of money, and if something bad happens, they get money to help them.
examples: I have fire insurance for my house.

senses.gloss: An instrument is any thing people hold in their hand and use to do something.
examples: A hammer is a heavy instrument.

senses.gloss: An instrument is something used to play music.
examples: I enjoy playing music, my favorite instrument is the guitar.

senses.gloss: To grow; to become bigger.
examples: The amount of money in my bank account is increasing.

senses.gloss: The amount which something has grown.
examples: There was an increase in movie releases last year.

senses.gloss: An industry is a kind of work that makes things.
examples: Many people in this country have jobs in the clothing industry.

senses.gloss: Industry is the quality of working hard, trying hard and doing it well.
examples: Because of her industry, she made a lot of money.

senses.gloss: Humor is ideas that make people laugh: jokes, funny things.
examples: I like the stories she tells because they're full of humor.
