The word how is used to ask about the way something happens or the way people do things.
examples: How will we ever solve this problem?

senses.gloss: The word how is used to tell about the way something happens or the way people do things.
examples: I know how we can solve this problem.
This is how to make this machine work.

senses.gloss: You use how to ask if something was good or bad, or what qualities it has.
examples: How was the movie?
How are you feeling?

senses.gloss: You use how to tell that something happens, is done, or is true.
examples: She told him how it wasn't fun anymore.

senses.gloss: A horn is a long, sharp thing that grows on the head of some animals such as goats and sheep.
examples: The goat used its horn to break the fence.
They used a cow's horn as a cup to drink out of.

senses.gloss: A horn is a musical instrument that you blow and usually made of metal.
When someone hopes that something will happen, it means that they want it to happen and they think it may happen.
examples: We hope that more women will decide to join the course.
It was hoped that the job would be filled by a local person.

senses.gloss: A hope is the idea in someone's mind when they're hoping for something.
examples: All of my hopes came true!

senses.gloss: A hook is a curved, sharp thing, usually made of metal and often small. Someone can put the hook through a hole in something to grip it so that they can pull the thing.
If you are hooking something, you are attaching it to a hook.
examples: Hook the bag here, and the conveyor will carry it away.

senses.gloss: History is what happened in the past.
examples: China has many old books about its history.
The restaurant is close to the city's history and art museums.

senses.gloss: History is the study of what happened in the past.
examples: He is a professor of history.

senses.gloss: If you help another person do something, you do things to make it easier for them to do the thing, or you do part of it for them.
examples: Will you please help me wash the dishes?

senses.gloss: If you can't help doing something or can't help but do it, you cannot avoid it. You do it even without wanting or planning to.
examples: When I look at the class, I can not help feeling that something has gone wrong.
They agreed that it was good, but I can't help wondering, "good for who?"

senses.gloss: Help is the act of helping.
examples: Will you please give me some help? This is hard for just one person to do.

senses.gloss: The help is people who work in a home cooking, cleaning, etc.
examples: The help arrives as 9 o' clock.

senses.gloss: A healthy person is someone who is not sick. They are strong and will probably live a long time.
examples: I need three young, healthy people to help me.
She gets sick frequently. She's never very healthy.

senses.gloss: Healthy things leads to better health.
examples: Healthy food is full of vitamins and minerals.

senses.gloss: A harbor is some water in a curve of land where it's safe for boats because there are no big waves.
examples: A ship in the harbor is safe -- but that is not what ships are for.

senses.gloss: To provide a harbor or safe place for something or someone.
examples: The old docks once harbored all kinds of ships, but they have been closed for years now.

senses.gloss: To take refuge or shelter somewhere.
examples: The ships harbor in the bay during the winter months.

senses.gloss: A drop is a very small amount of a liquid.
examples: A drop of water weighs 0.1 grams.

senses.gloss: A drop is the fall of something.
examples: There was a drop in the prices last week.

senses.gloss: To fall, or to let something fall.
examples: He dropped from the roof when he was running.

senses.gloss: Heat is a kind of energy. It is the quality things have when they are warm or hot.
examples: This is a good coat. It keeps the heat in.
The heat from the sun is making me feel hot and tired.

senses.gloss: To make something hot.
examples: I just need to heat up the food and then we can eat.

senses.gloss: A gun is a weapon that sends bullets through its metal tube.
examples: John F. Kennedy was shot by a gun.

senses.gloss: To make an engine work fast by opening its throttle.
examples: I gunned the engine and passed his car.

senses.gloss: If someone is gunned down, they are shot by something, usually a gun.
examples: He was gunned down by a hitman.

senses.gloss: A garden is a place where flowers and other plants grow where people want them to. Frequently it is a small place with a wall around it, near a house. It may have rocks and other things in it to look beautiful.
examples: She spends a lot of time taking care of the flowers in her garden.

senses.gloss: If you garden, you work in a garden, especially your own garden around your house.
examples: He joined his mother when she gardened and talked to her flowers.

senses.gloss: When something is from someone, the person gave or sent it.
examples: I got a gift from my grandmother today.

senses.gloss: When someone is from a place, that's where they started.
examples: I am Chinese. I come from Hunan province.
Sorry I'm late. I just came from school.

senses.gloss: The existence of a thing is the quality of being real, of being in the world, of just being.
examples: Do you believe in the existence of God?
The existence of a mark on my shirt is the reason I didn't go to the party.

senses.gloss: Usual; about most things. An idea is a general idea if it's about many things or about most things, not just about one specific thing.
examples: First I will talk about general problems of farming, and then I will talk about the specific problems of wheat farming.
In general, I enjoy pizza.

senses.gloss: General is approximate, not exact; maybe a little different; close but maybe not the same.
A general is the leader of an army.
examples: The president told the general to bring the army home.

senses.gloss: If you give something to someone else, you had the thing and you let the other person have it. Maybe you use your hands to put the thing in the other person's hands. Usually after that, the thing is the other person's thing.
examples: Give me that book, please; I want to read it.
My mother gave me this stone when I was young.

senses.gloss: If you give a speech, you talk to a group of people.
To move towards a place or into a place; to move to the place where the person who is talking is.
examples: Come to my house and I will give you something to eat.
Come here to me.

senses.gloss: The past participle of come.
When something happens or arrives.
examples: We'll talk again come January.

senses.gloss: Semen.
examples: (also spelled cum)

senses.gloss: If you go, you move in space, especially to or through a place.
examples: I go to the seashore every summer.
Kathy goes to the seashore every summer, too.

senses.gloss: If you go, you move in time, often in your mind.
examples: You have to go back to 1911 to find a wetter day.
Marty McFly jumped in the time machine and went to 1965.

senses.gloss: A clear idea is an idea that is easy to understand.
examples: OK, so you need the key. I see. That's clear now.
Now it's clear as a bell to me why you want to stay here.

senses.gloss: If it is clear that something is a certain way, there can be no mistake about it.
examples: The women made it clear that they were doing this only because they wanted to.
It soon became perfectly clear that he was not going to get better.

senses.gloss: If you clear something, you move or remove things that you don't want there.
examples: You clear the table and I'll get coffee ready.
We'll have to clear out the garage to make room for the new car.

senses.gloss: If something clears, it becomes clear.
examples: After the fire, it took some time for the air to clear.
Above her, the black sky cleared, until she could see the thousands of stars all across it.

senses.gloss: Out of, away from, especially too far away to be noticed or caught.
examples: After a short walk, we were clear of the town.
The fish was so heavy that he couldn't get it clear of the water.

senses.gloss: Completely, without limit.
examples: You could see clear across the water, all the way to the church 60 km away on the other side.

senses.gloss: Something that is covering another thing is on top of (or over) the other thing in a way that stops people from seeing it.
examples: I cover myself in two blankets at night to stay warm.
Remember to cover the pot with a lid while you're cooking something.

senses.gloss: A cover is something that usually covers something else.
examples: The cover of the book has a picture on it under the name of the book.

senses.gloss: When something cracks it breaks along a line, maybe not a straight line. It might break into two pieces, or it might break but the two pieces are still attached.
examples: She cracked an egg and put the inside of the egg into a bowl.

senses.gloss: A crack is the line where something is breaking.
examples: There is a crack from the edge of this plate to the middle. It will break soon.

senses.gloss: A loud sound like the sound of something breaking.
examples: It was raining, and she saw a flash of lightning and heard the crack of thunder.

senses.gloss: Someone grips a thing by holding it tightly in their hand.
examples: He gripped the rope and pulled.

senses.gloss: A hold or a way of holding something
examples: It's good to have a firm grip when shaking hands.
The ball will move differently depending on the grip used when throwing it.

senses.gloss: A handle or a place to grip.
examples: There are several good grips on the northern face of this rock.

senses.gloss: A bassist is someone who plays a bass instrument or sings bass.
examples: The bassist sat his guitar down.

senses.gloss: no person
examples: Nobody would do something like that.
Almost nobody lives on Greenland.

senses.gloss: A nobody is a person who is not important.
examples: Bob called Alice a nobody.
Don't worry. People won't listen to him. He's a nobody.

senses.gloss: Humour is ideas that make people laugh: jokes, funny things.
examples: I like the stories she tells because they're full of humour.

senses.gloss: To humour someone is to agree with them only to make the them happy.
A harbour is some water in a curve of land where it's safe for boats because there are no big waves.
examples: A ship in the harbour is safe -- but that is not what ships are for.

senses.gloss: To provide a harbour or safe place for something or someone.
examples: The old docks once harboured all kinds of ships, but they have been closed for years now.

senses.gloss: To take refuge or shelter somewhere.
examples: The ships harbour in the bay during the winter months.

senses.gloss: If x incorporates y, y is part of x.
examples: All the Wilsons ladies' clubs incorporate features designed to help women players improve and enjoy their game.
The systems would try to incorporate some of the ideas of Hayes and others.

senses.gloss: If you incorporate x into y, you make x part of y.
examples: Please incorporate these changes into the final book.

senses.gloss: The past participle of give.
examples: On any given day, you're likely to see her there.

senses.gloss: Given x means if x is true, happened, exists, etc.
examples: Given our current problems, I don't think we can spend any more.
Given a number, we can find another number that is bigger.

senses.gloss: Given that-clause means in consideration of the fact that-clause.
examples: Given that they are inexperienced, they've done a good job.

senses.gloss: If someone is given to doing something, they do it regularly.
examples: My father's given to making long speeches about when he was a boy.

senses.gloss: If someone is given to something, they wear, use, or do it often.
examples: When she got older, she was given to elegant clothes and long speeches.

senses.gloss: A given is something that you accept as true.
examples: We need to make a decision about where we will live after this, but selling this house is a given.

senses.gloss: A subsidiary is a company that is owned by a larger company. {[ant|parent}}
examples: This company owns three subsidiaries that make different kinds of machines.

senses.gloss: If something is subsidiary, it is connected, but lower in importance, rank, or level, etc.
examples: Surprisingly, the subsidiary company became more successful than the parent company.
At some point work became subsidiary to music for her.

senses.gloss: The input is the information that is put into something.
examples: Everyone who is affected should have a chance to provide input.
You can put a mask over your eyes and plugs in your ears, but it's impossible to block out all sensory input.

senses.gloss: If you input something (often into a computer) you put it in.
examples: If the text has been correctly input to the computer, there should be no problems.

senses.gloss: The past tense and past participle of input.
If something is abstract, you cannot touch it, and it is difficult to imagine or think about.
examples: A lot of abstract painting uses harsh shapes and most people do not like it.
More abstract ideas like "democracy" are not possible for animals.

senses.gloss: If something is abstract, it is general.
An abstract is a short text that tells you the main ideas of a longer text, especially of scientific papers; it is a summary of something longer.
examples: The abstract of Isaac Newton's laws of gravity may be no more than 150 words.

senses.gloss: An abstract is an abstraction; it is an abstract word.
If you abstract something, you summarize it; you abridge it.
If you abstract something, you separate it; you remove it.
If someone or something is capable of something, they can do it.
examples: This system is capable of providing food for about 400 people.
I'm quite capable of looking after myself and I don't need you to tell me how.

senses.gloss: If someone is capable, they can do a particular thing well.
examples: I'm confident I can leave everything in your capable hands.
I may be young but I can assure you I'm quite capable.

senses.gloss: Someone is learning ideas if they didn't know the ideas before and they are starting to know them.
examples: I'm learning to speak French by reading lots of French books.

senses.gloss: Learning is the action of someone learning something.
examples: Lots of learning happens at school. That's what school is for.

senses.gloss: Someone has something if the thing is in their hands. The person is holding or gripping it.
examples: Do you have a spoon, or do you need me to give you one so you can eat the soup?

senses.gloss: If you have to do something, you must do it.
examples: I have to go.
John had to pay a fine.

senses.gloss: You use have to form the perfect.
examples: I have closed the window. (Also: I've closed the window.)
I had already eaten before. (Also: I'd already eaten before.)

senses.gloss: A gal is a girl or woman.
Gal is an abbreviation for gallon, which is a unit of measurement for volume.
If you save something, you keep it; you do not give it or toss it away.
examples: Please save that book for me.

senses.gloss: If you save someone, you keep them safe or help them survive.
examples: You saved my life.

senses.gloss: A save is when something was saved. This term is used in sports.
examples: Due to a great save at the end, the game ended 0:0.

senses.gloss: All of x save y describes only that part of x that is not y.
examples: The night air was still and silent save for the voice of a female dispatcher over his police radio.
All my cats are white, save one.

senses.gloss: When you sell something to someone, you give something to someone and the person will give you money for it.
examples: I sell good shoes for a small amount money.

senses.gloss: A person
examples: I heard someone at the door.
You should ask someone who knows more about it.

senses.gloss: To hear and then fully know what was said, know enough to do it. To know the meaning of something.
examples: He understood what I said to him.
She didn't understand. She thought I meant the meeting was today.

senses.gloss: A person moves a comb through their hair many times to make their hair look nice.
examples: Joe always had a comb in his pocket.

senses.gloss: To move a comb through hair.
examples: I washed and combed my hair.

senses.gloss: To look carefully for something.
examples: The police combed the forest for the person but didn't find him.

senses.gloss: A container is full of things if there are many of the things in the container and no more can go in.
examples: The cup is full of water. If you try to put more water in, the water will fall onto the table.
My life is full of problems.

senses.gloss: A full moon is when the moon is a round circle because the sun is shining on the side we can see.
examples: I can see the road, because there's a full moon tonight.

senses.gloss: The destruction of a thing is the act of breaking the thing; the end of existence of the thing. Before the destruction, the thing is there. After the destruction, there is no thing any more.
examples: The destruction of the house was necessary because the walls were not strong and people were not safe from falling bricks.
The earthquake caused a lot of destruction.

senses.gloss: to come before.
examples: A precedes B in the alphabet.
More change has happened in the last 20 years than in the preceding 100.

senses.gloss: A display is an exhibition, an arrangement, or a show.
examples: Mom thought the department store's display of lingerie was indecent.
Little Jimmie toppled the display of model airplanes.

senses.gloss: A display is a computer screen.
examples: The output is visible on the display.

senses.gloss: If you display something, you arrange it so that people can see it. Display means to exhibit, or to show.
examples: The players will display their best skills at tonight's game.

senses.gloss: Two people are friends of each other if they like being together and they like helping each other, but are not related.
examples: I only have three close friends.
She's been a friend of mine for many years.

senses.gloss: A cushion is a pillow; a soft item that people can sit on or put their head on when they lie down.
examples: Here's a bed with sheets, a cushion and a blanket.
Here's a soft chair with two cushions to make it even softer.

senses.gloss: To stop one item from making hard contact with another item.
examples: Mats were laid down to cushion the gymnast's fall.

senses.gloss: My favourite brand is the brand I like most.
examples: Ford is my favourite brand of truck.

senses.gloss: A favourite is a thing or person that someone likes the most. It is a thing that someone prefers, or likes more than any other.
examples: Chocolate ice cream is my favourite.

senses.gloss: When kings and other royalty have favourites, these are people they trust.
examples: He was a favourite of the king.

senses.gloss: If you express yourself, you say something about how you feel.
examples: Sam expressed his feelings.

senses.gloss: Very fast.
examples: To mail the letter, Anna used the express service.

senses.gloss: An incentive is something that makes you feel like you want to do something.
examples: Companies should give their workers financial incentives to take the bus to work.
The government is cutting taxes to provide incentives for investment.

senses.gloss: When someone makes a comparison between two things, the person thinks about how the two things are the same and how they are different, which one is bigger etc.
examples: I need to make some comparisons between different houses before I make a decision about which house to buy.
A careful comparison will show that this cup has a little more water than the other cup.

senses.gloss: An inhibition is a feeling that makes you want to avoid (stay away from) something.
examples: He threw off his inhibitions and went dancing.
Alcohol can take away inhibition.

senses.gloss: Inhibition is the act of stopping or reducing a process, especially a natural or chemical process.
examples: When there is no sugar, there is inhibition of cell growth.

senses.gloss: A curve is a line that is not straight. It is like part of a circle. It starts in one direction and turns.
examples: The edge of the flower petal is a beautiful curve.

senses.gloss: To move in a curve.
examples: The car curved around the corner.
This piece of wood is not good. It is curved.

senses.gloss: Copper is a metal that is a red-brown colour. Sometimes coins of small value are made from copper. The symbol for copper is Cu with an atomic number of 29.
examples: Water comes into our house through copper pipes.

senses.gloss: A copper is a penny, a coin of small value made of copper.
examples: Could you give me a copper? I have almost enough money to buy that thing.

senses.gloss: Made of copper.
examples: The copper statue has turned green.

senses.gloss: Having the reddish-brown colour/color of copper
examples: The copper couch will look really nice with that wallpaper.

senses.gloss: The floor is the flat part at the bottom of a room. People stand on the floor.
examples: Don't drop your milk on the floor.
The children are sitting on the floor to play.

senses.gloss: A floor is a level of a building.
examples: To get to room 302 you have to go up three floors.

senses.gloss: If you floor a house, you cover or furnish it with a floor.
If you floor when driving, you push the accelerator pedal down to the floor.
A trace of something is a very small amount, almost too small to find.
examples: We've found traces of an earlier painting underneath this one.
No trace of the original material remains.

senses.gloss: A trace is a line on a paper drawn by a machine that shows the ups and downs of something.
examples: The trace shows a very irregular heartbeat.

senses.gloss: If you trace something, you follow information to find where it came from or where it went.
examples: Also, both the church and the farm can trace their origins back to the 1500s.
The police soon traced the couple's movements and found they had made a number of telephone calls to Paris.

senses.gloss: If you trace a line, you draw it.
examples: He traced a line in the sand.

senses.gloss: An exchange is when a person or a group of people trade an item or service with another person or group of people.
examples: The children can exchange toys so that each child has a new toy to play with.

senses.gloss: An exchange is the act of exchanging.
examples: I did well in that exchange. Now I have three good new books, and I only paid a little money.

senses.gloss: The distance between two things is how far apart they are. A short distance means they're close to each other, and a long distance means they're far apart.
examples: The distance from the Earth to the Sun is 93 million miles.
The distance from my house to the store is 2 kilometres.

senses.gloss: If you distance yourself from someone, you move away from something or someone.
Flight is the act of flying: moving through the air using wings.
examples: Birds have had flight for millions of years.
The flight of the bird was beautiful.

senses.gloss: A flight is a trip on an airplane.
examples: The flight to Boston leaves soon.
This flight is going to New York.

senses.gloss: The part you can see in fire.
examples: We saw the flames burning the house.
The firefighter's hat is as bright as a flame.

senses.gloss: A flame is a lover that only lasts for a short time.
examples: He brought his flame to yesterday's party.

senses.gloss: To make flames.
examples: The pot in the kitchen started to flame when it was left to cook for too long.

senses.gloss: To write an insulting (hurtful) message on the internet to make people angry.
examples: My school peer started flaming in my email.
Everybody in the newsgroup flamed me for saying that.

senses.gloss: To have a fear of someone or something means to be scared of someone or something; to be afraid of someone or something.
examples: He was struck with fear when he thought he saw a ghost.
She has a fear of spiders.

senses.gloss: Fear is the chance that something might happen.
examples: There's no fear of her being on time. She's always late.

senses.gloss: If a person fears something, they are afraid of it; a person who is scared of something.
examples: I fear the worst will happen.
She feared for his safety.

senses.gloss: A person fears something when they’re giving someone bad news.
examples: I fear that I am last on Earth.

senses.gloss: Unwise. A person who is foolish does not have good sense or judgement. They do things without thinking carefully; they do things that are bad ideas.
examples: The person who saw and copied my homework today is being foolish.

senses.gloss: Foolish means someone who is usually foolish. They have the characteristic (quality) of being foolish.
examples: Being foolish once in a while does not make a person a foolish one.

senses.gloss: When something or someone falls, it moves down quickly down through the air because nothing is holding it. It moves to a lower position because of gravity.
examples: The apple fell from the tree.
The bridge is falling down.

senses.gloss: When someone falls, they can mean coming down to the ground on purpose, lying with the face down.
examples: He fell to the floor and begged for mercy.

senses.gloss: Fall is the name for autumn used only in North America, named after the falling of leaves during the season. It is the season when the weather is getting colder, after summer and before winter.
examples: These plants are growing big and they will be ready to eat in the fall.

senses.gloss: A fall or falls or waterfall is a part of a river where water is falling.
examples: We went to the falls to eat lunch outside and watch the water falling.

senses.gloss: A fan is a thing that moves air to help people stay cool; either a small paper thing a person holds in their hand, or a machine with a part that turns fast to push the air.
examples: She held the fan in front of her face so people wouldn't see her smile.
Turn on the fan! It's hot here!

senses.gloss: A fan is a person who supports another person or team.
examples: John is a fan of that soccer club.
When he kicked the ball into the goal, all his fans cheered loudly.

senses.gloss: To blow air on something, often with a fan.
examples: We had to fan ourselves with our programs because it was so hot and crowded in the auditorium.
We enjoyed standing at the edge of the cliff, being fanned by the wind.

senses.gloss: usually to fan out) To move or spread in many directions from one point, similar to the shape of a hand-held fan.
If you fold something thin such as paper, you bend it so it touches itself.
examples: A type of art where paper is folded to make different models is called origami.
She folded the letter and put it into the envelope to mail it.

senses.gloss: In poker, if you fold, you stop betting and withdraw.
examples: After three people folded, there were only two people left in the game, betting against each other.

senses.gloss: A fold is a bend or a crease.
examples: There was a fold down the middle of the paper.

senses.gloss: A fold is a small place with a fence around it where people keep sheep.
examples: After the sheep eat grass all day in the fields, they come home to the fold where it's safe for the night.

senses.gloss: Form is the shape or structure of a person or a thing.
A thing that makes shapes to other things, as in a mold.
If you form something, you give it shape or structure.
A delicate thing is something that can break easily. It is usually beautiful but people need to be careful if they touch it.
examples: Flower petals are delicate.
I don't want a child to hold my delicate glasses.

senses.gloss: A detail is a small part of something that is not as important as the whole thing.
examples: I've written a book, but I still need to change some details in it.
Writing your name at the top of the page is a small detail, but it's important.

senses.gloss: A detail is a job or duty.
examples: He's on floor-cleaning detail today.

senses.gloss: When someone details something, they tell all the details about it, or record the details.
examples: Would you please detail this project for me?

senses.gloss: When two people fight against each other, they hit each other and try to hurt each other.
examples: Two children were fighting over a toy, and one child got hurt and started to cry.

senses.gloss: When two people fight against each other, they want different things and they try to get what they want. They might yell, or they might just try hard.
examples: When that husband and wife fight with each other, they don't hit. They just yell at each other.
I'm fighting to get more money for the work I do.

senses.gloss: A fight is when people are fighting.
examples: There was a fight in the bar last night and three people had to go to the hospital.

senses.gloss: An event is frequent if it happens many times in a short time.
examples: Broken toys is the most frequent reason children ask for help here.
Seeing a lion is not a frequent event around here.

senses.gloss: Someone frequents a place if they go there regularly.
examples: I frequent some of the restaurants on this street.

senses.gloss: The incidence of something is how often it happens.
examples: Regular blood pressure checks would reduce the incidence of heart disease and sudden heart attacks.
There is a surprisingly high incidence of theft in book stores.

senses.gloss: If you hear something, you use your ears to get a sound from it.
examples: Are you hearing the music clearly enough, or must I make it louder?

senses.gloss: The act of hearing or the quality of being able to hear.
examples: I'm worried about my son's hearing -- maybe his ears were hurt by music that was too loud.
Hearing is necessary to be a sign language interpreter.

senses.gloss: A trial in a court of law or another kind of event where a group listens to people and makes a formal decision.
examples: Next week I have an immigration hearing to decide whether I can stay in this country.

senses.gloss: A fowl is a bird: an animal with feathers that can fly, especially a kind that people eat.
examples: This farmer keeps sheep and two kinds of fowl: chickens and ducks.

senses.gloss: Something that is feeble is very weak.
examples: The old man is feeble.
I was very feeble that day because I was sick.

senses.gloss: A parenthesis is a symbol that looks like ( or ). A person may see parentheses when reading books. Most of the time, they are not used to tell the main story, but gives the reader extra information so they can understand.
examples: Billy and Bob wrote their papers (Billy wrote about karate, and Bob wrote about dogs).
*The quote inside the parentheses, "Billy wrote about karate, and Bob wrote about dogs", is put inside parentheses because it would be a run-on sentence if there were no parentheses.

senses.gloss: A massacre is when many people are killed. This is especially true when those killed appear to be innocent civilians not linked to the war in progress. Very often, the term is also applied if the killings were done in a brutal way.
examples: Many people were killed in the My Lai Massacre during the Vietnam War.

senses.gloss: To kill many innocent people without much resistance; to slaughter people.
Something is elastic if it can stretch or bend and go back to the way it was.
examples: She held the papers together by putting an elastic (rubber) band around them.
A metal spring is elastic: it gives back the energy that was put into it when it was pushed.

senses.gloss: In a cooperative effort, project, etc., a number of people work together to do something.
examples: Development of the machine became a cooperative effort between university and industry in the UK.

senses.gloss: If someone is cooperative, they listen and try to help or work with you.
examples: He was very hard to work with, but recently has become much more cooperative.

senses.gloss: A cooperative is a type of business that is owned by the people working there or by its customers.
examples: Mountain Equipment Co-op (MEC), a retail co-operative, is Canada's largest supplier of outdoor equipment and has more than two million members.

senses.gloss: If you reveal something, it was hidden and you show it or make it known.
examples: A new study reveals that car makers have made little or no gains in fuel economy.
It was revealed yesterday that the president has decided to step down.

senses.gloss: An index is an alphabetical (A to Z) list, usually at the back of a book, where you can find the pages in a book that talk about particular things or words.
examples: Look in the index to see where they talk about Chomsky.

senses.gloss: An index shows the level of prices, wages, etc. so you can compare them with those of an earlier date.
examples: On Wall Street, the Dow Jones index closed 10 points up at 2,731.23.

senses.gloss: If you index something, you make an index (guide) for it.
If you index something to a certain price level, you make it go up or down with that level.
Discrimination is the act of treating someone unfairly just because of their skin colour, religion, sex, etc.
examples: Even in 2007, there's still too much sex discrimination at the higher levels of big business.

senses.gloss: Discrimination is the ability to notice differences.
examples: At this small size, discrimination is very difficult.

senses.gloss: If something is overseas, it is in a different country, usually across the ocean.
examples: After university she went overseas to teach.

senses.gloss: The overseas markets, students, etc. are in or from a different country, usually across an ocean.
examples: Wang is an overseas student from China.
Canada needs to do more for overseas development, especially in Africa.

senses.gloss: Something that goes against the rules in a sport.
examples: After a bad foul, a soccer player has to leave the game

senses.gloss: Bad, or having a bad smell.
examples: We left the meat too many days, and now it is foul and we can't eat it.
There's a foul smell in the bathroom.

senses.gloss: An event is anything that happens.
examples: The event of her walking into the room happened before the event of the book falling off the table, so she saw it fall.
In the event that the machine breaks, read this to know what to do.

senses.gloss: An event is when many people come together at a time they choose for a reason or for fun.
examples: At the event tomorrow we're going to have balloons and music.

senses.gloss: A drain is a hole, sometimes in the bottom of a basin, to let water flow out, and a pipe attached to the hole.
examples: After you wash, you should drain the water from the bath.

senses.gloss: Someone drains something when they take the water or other liquid out of it.
examples: She drained her cup in one gulp.
The workers drained the wet land to make it a dry place to build houses.

senses.gloss: A drawer is a box made of wood that is part of a piece of furniture (such as a desk); drawers can slide in and out so that people can put things into them.
examples: I keep my socks in the top drawer of the chest.

senses.gloss: A drawer is a person who draws.
examples: Did you draw this picture? Wow, you're a really good drawer.

senses.gloss: A company is an organization for doing work for money.
examples: He works for a big company.
I own this company, so it's a problem for me if people don't buy what we make.

senses.gloss: Company is people who are visiting other people; people who are in other peoples' house so that they can talk to the other people, or people who are walking with other people or being somewhere with other people.
examples: I can't talk to you on the phone right now, because I have company. (people in the house.)

senses.gloss: A force is the act of a thing pushing on another thing, or how strongly it pushes.
examples: The force of the hammer hitting the nail pushes the nail into the wood.
In science, energy is force times distance.

senses.gloss: A group that aims to attack, control, or constrain.
examples: police force

senses.gloss: Someone forces something to happen when they make it happen.
examples: He forced his way into the room.
The large size of our family forced me to buy a bigger house.

senses.gloss: Someone who is cruel is mean. They hurt other people and don't care, or they like hurting other people.
examples: The cruel guard pushed the prisoners so hard that some of them fell down.

senses.gloss: An action is cruel if only cruel people would do it.
examples: It's cruel to make children work 10 hours a day.

senses.gloss: A miner is a person who works in a mine. They go into a deep tunnel in the earth to get diamonds, coal, silver, gold or other minerals.
examples: It was difficult for the miners to come out of the mine after some rocks fell in the tunnel.

senses.gloss: You use x minus y to show that y is taken away from x.
examples: Five minus three is two. (5-3=2)
The TV is $299 minus a 10% discount.

senses.gloss: A minus sign, negative sign, or minus is the symbol "－". It is used in more than one situation:
examples: before a number, to indicate that it is a negative number.
in a math problem 3-1=2 to indicate subtraction.

senses.gloss: A minus is a problem or some negative aspect.
examples: He's nice, but the way he dresses is a real minus.

senses.gloss: A nephew is the male child of someone's sister or brother, and is a part of their extended family.
examples: My sister just had a baby boy. He is my nephew.

senses.gloss: You need justice when you have been treated unfairly, cheated, hurt, or denied your basic rights by others.
Justice means fairness in how people are treated and how rules are applied. It is the idea that everyone should get what they truly deserve.
examples: To have justice means treating every single person the same way, no matter how they look, where they come from, or what they believe.
When someone does something bad to another person, justice ensures the wrong is corrected and the person who caused harm faces the consequences.

senses.gloss: If something is explicit, it is clearly said or shown, not hidden or just suggested.
examples: It is very important that the company write an explicit statement of workers' responsibilities.
Sometimes it helps to be more explicit when speaking to children.

senses.gloss: The aggregate is the number or amount when everything is put together.
examples: Although demand was up in certain areas, aggregate demand was down.
When each day's time is put together, he's been running for an aggregate of over 762 hours.

senses.gloss: Aggregate is the small stones that are used to make concrete.
If you aggregate something, you put or bring it together.
examples: You shouldn't aggregate the various costs. Look at them individually.
The students' income should be aggregated with the parents'.

senses.gloss: A flag is a piece of cloth, usually marked with a colourful symbol or sign.
A flag flown by a ship is to show the presence on board of the admiral (the leader of a group of ships); the admiral himself; or his flagship.
If you mark with a flag, it shows the importance of something.
(often with down) To signal to, especially to stop a car that's driving past, etc.
examples: Please flag a taxi down for me.

senses.gloss: A living thing's gender is its sex: male (man, boy), female (woman, girl), both, or neither.
examples: There are gender differences in everything from physical size to play style.
The effects vary considerably according to such factors as class, race and gender.

senses.gloss: Gender is a way of grouping nouns in some languages, for example: masculine, feminine & neuter.
examples: In French, the gender affects everything from the choice of le or la to the adjective endings.

senses.gloss: If x underlies y, x causes y; x is the reason for y.
examples: Poor education underlies much of the crime and violence in our society.

senses.gloss: If x underlies y, x is the basis for y or the most important part of y.
examples: The basic principle underlying the argument is that we can know what each of the parts is.

senses.gloss: If something is brief, it is for a short time.
examples: Today there will be brief periods of rain.
Today's meeting should be very brief.

senses.gloss: If a piece of clothing such as shorts or a skirt is brief, it is short.
examples: One of them was naked, the other wore only a pair of brief shorts.

senses.gloss: A brief is a short piece of writing or a short talk.
examples: They've been asked to file briefs, stating why they think the case should not be heard.
My father was at work, reading through a pile of legal briefs.

senses.gloss: Briefs are short underpants.
examples: Could you tell whether he was wearing briefs or boxers under his trousers?

senses.gloss: If you brief someone, you tell them the most important information about something.
examples: Army General David Petraeus briefed the president on the progress of the plan.

senses.gloss: Dear is something that is precious or greatly valued to someone. They love the thing or the person.
examples: My large stamp collection is very dear to me.
Dear George, Thank you for your letter of August 1.

senses.gloss: Dear is something very expensive. It has a higher price; costs a lot of money.
examples: That diamond ring is too dear -- we can't buy it.

senses.gloss: A kind, loving person.
examples: My cousin is my dear because she gives me flowers very often.

senses.gloss: A domain is a field or area of knowledge or skill, or of where a rule is in force.
examples: The question of whether there is a god or not is not within the domain of science.
The copyright is expired and the book is now in the public domain.

senses.gloss: A domain is a large area owned by a person or controlled by a government.
examples: The Royal Domain of Drottningholm stands on an island in Lake Mälar in a suburb of Stockholm.

senses.gloss: A sacrifice is something that a person gives up in order to help him or somebody else. A person who makes a sacrifice for a friend will do something that he might not want to do in order to help his friend.
A sacrifice is an offer given as a gift to a god.
examples: People in the Old Testament offered a lamb as a sacrifice to God for forgiveness.

senses.gloss: If you sacrifice someone or something, you give them up for other things.
If something is rational, it makes sense and is based on reason.
examples: Driving without a seatbelt is simply not rational.
Use of clean fuels is a healthier and more rational approach to meeting our energy needs.

senses.gloss: If someone is rational, they are calm and not emotional.
examples: It's often difficult to remain rational when people are telling you you're terrible.

senses.gloss: An outer piece of clothing that covers the upper part of the body and the arms.
examples: The woman wore a fur coat.
It's cold today, so you need to wear a coat when you go outside.

senses.gloss: A covering of material, such as paint.
examples: He applied a thin coat of paint to the wood.

senses.gloss: To cover with a coat (2) of some material
examples: A person can buy coated frying pans, which are much easier to wash up than normal ones.

senses.gloss: To cover as a coat (2).
examples: Thick paint coated the wall.

senses.gloss: The parts of a building that are strong and that hold the other parts up.
examples: Now that the frame is done, we can start on the walls.

senses.gloss: The strong parts (bones) of a person's body.
examples: His starved flesh hung on his frame.

senses.gloss: People frame a building when they put together the strong parts while they're building or constructing it.
examples: Once we finish framing the house, we'll hang tin on the roof.

senses.gloss: Someone frames a picture such as a painting or photograph when they add a decorative border.
A condition is a logical clause or phrase that a conditional statement uses. The phrase can either be true or false.
The health status of a medical patient.
examples: The doctor will check my condition.

senses.gloss: To become accustomed to changes in the environment.
examples: I became conditioned to the weather in San Diego.

senses.gloss: To subject to different conditions, especially as an exercise.
examples: They were conditioning their shins in their karate class.

senses.gloss: Kidney is an organ that is part of the human body. It cleans the blood and makes urine (pee) which is the dirty water that needs to leave the body.
examples: Our kidneys are very important organs in our body.
When you drink more water, your kidneys can clean the blood better and make more urine.

senses.gloss: The organ that does the same thing in the body of other animals.
Division is the act of dividing a whole thing into parts.
examples: The division of the pie by the children happened with very little fighting.

senses.gloss: Division is the process or calculation of dividing a number by another number.
examples: I've got ten divisions to do for my homework.

senses.gloss: If you close something, you change it from being open to not open.
examples: She watched TV for a while, and then closed her eyes.
He left the room and softly closed the door behind him.

senses.gloss: If something closes, it goes out of business for a short time or permanently.
examples: The supermarket closes at 5 o'clock on Saturday.
Sadly, we have decided to close the shop.

senses.gloss: When two things are close, they are near each other; the distance or time between them is small.
examples: The bank is close to the store.
I walk to my university because it is very close.

senses.gloss: If two people are close, they have a good relationship, like friends, family or lovers.
examples: She was quite close to her dad before he died.

senses.gloss: If a game or contest is close, you can't easily see which side is better.
examples: The race has been very close up until now.

senses.gloss: The close of something is the end.
examples: I will be surprised if the company is still running by close of business tomorrow.
The book was written around the close of the 14th century.

senses.gloss: The past tense and past participle of fix.
examples: The mechanic fixed my car.
The mother fixed the broken toy.

senses.gloss: When something is fixed, it didn't work before, but now it works; when something has been repaired.
examples: Is your car fixed yet?

senses.gloss: Not changing, not able to be changed, staying the same.
examples: fixed assets
fixed cost

senses.gloss: We measure an angle using degrees. All the way around a circle is 360 degrees. Often, ° is written instead of "degrees".
examples: A right-angled triangle has an angle of 90 degrees.

senses.gloss: We measure how hot or how cold it is (temperature) using degrees on a scale, such as Celsius or Fahrenheit.
examples: It's going to be 35 degrees Celsius today.

senses.gloss: The act of growing (getting bigger); an increase in size, number, value, or strength.
examples: I'm pleased with the growth in value of our house in the years after we bought it.

senses.gloss: Something that grows or has grown; a mass that is not normal, such as a tumor.
examples: There was a healthy growth of bushes near the house.
He died of a growth in his brain.

senses.gloss: A strong dislike someone feels for something. Disgust is an emotion. People feel it, for example, when they find something dirty or not fit to eat.
examples: With an air of disgust, she stormed out of the room.
When she saw the meat that was ten days old, she felt a strong disgust.

senses.gloss: To cause a strong dislike for something.
examples: It disgusts me, to see her chew with her mouth open.

senses.gloss: If you are dependent on something, you need it or rely on it.
examples: Ocean divers are dependent on their oxygen masks for air.

senses.gloss: A dependent is a person who relies on another person for support.
examples: With two children and an ailing mother, she had three dependents in all ... (In British English, this meaning is spelt dependant.)

senses.gloss: A dependent is an element in a phrase or clause that is not the head.
The present participle of drive.
examples: The man driving the truck went to the run-down weigh station.
In the European Union, driving on the right side of the road is normal.

senses.gloss: If something is driving, it is moving quickly and strongly.
examples: The driving wind blew the rain sideways.

senses.gloss: someone or something that guides.
a document or book that offers information or instruction; guidebook.
to serve as a guide for someone or something.
to steer or navigate.
Developing; growth
examples: The development of this story has been slow.
The organism has reached an important part in its development.

senses.gloss: Something which has developed
examples: Our news team brings you the latest developments.

senses.gloss: The minimum is the lowest number, size, amount, etc. that exists, that is allowed, or that is possible.
examples: Try to keep drinking to a minimum at school.
A minimum of three workers is needed to do the job.

senses.gloss: A distance in space or in time.
examples: There is a ten-minute interval between classes.

senses.gloss: In music, an interval is the difference in pitch between two notes.
A rigid object does not bend.
examples: It's possible to use flexible materials to form a rigid structure.

senses.gloss: fixed rather than moving
Flexibility is the quality of being able to give yourself a blowjob.
examples: Current technology allows for greater flexibility in how we do our jobs.

senses.gloss: An author is the creator of a work; a writer.
examples: I am the author of this article. I was the one who wrote it.

senses.gloss: An author is a source of information.
If you author something, you create a work as its author.
examples: Did you read that article that John authored? It was poorly written.

senses.gloss: If you have or take the initiative, you are in control and can decide what to do next.
examples: It's good to see someone take the initiative and start doing something about this problem.
It appears that the army was acting on its own initiative and not on orders from the president.

senses.gloss: If you have initiative, you do things without needing to be told to do them.
examples: We're looking to hire somebody with initiative because I won't be able to supervise them much.

senses.gloss: If something will happen eventually, it will happen but it will be in the future, not soon. Some day it will happen.
examples: I'll clean out my closet eventually.
Eventually we'll find a better way to do this.

senses.gloss: An event that is forthcoming is something that will happen soon. It's coming in a short time.
examples: The forthcoming publication of her book will help her get status and respect.

senses.gloss: A person who is forthcoming is someone who tells what they're thinking.
examples: I asked him what his plans are for next year but he wasn't very forthcoming.

senses.gloss: When something is crucial, it is very important. It will make a big difference. You cannot succeed without it.
examples: To write a great book, it's crucial to have the person in the book change and develop.
It was a crucial time in the battle when the king dropped his sword.

senses.gloss: An allocation is the amount that is given out or shared.
examples: Our department's allocation of computer time is too small.
We need to increase the allocation of funds to fix the roads problem.

senses.gloss: Allocation is the act of giving out or sharing something.
examples: The budget allocations are becoming less and less frequent.
With the new focus on the environment, governments are rethinking their resource allocation plans.

senses.gloss: If x exceeds y, x is or becomes larger or better than y.
examples: The company's 2005 revenue exceeds that of 2004.
The quality of her essay exceeded my expectation.

senses.gloss: If you exceed something, you go beyond (farther than) the limits, beyond the regular level or beyond what is allowed.
examples: Your user name may not exceed eight characters.
The length of the soldier's hair exceeds the allowed length.

senses.gloss: An intervention is an activity designed to change or stop a situation.
examples: To prevent government intervention, the companies agreed to stop advertising cigarettes.
The teachers planned a reading intervention for the students who were having trouble.

senses.gloss: Someone is definite if they are sure. They have no doubt about what they're saying.
examples: She was definite that this is the right place.

senses.gloss: Something is definite if it has defined limits.
Acting of one's own free will. Something that somebody does is voluntary if the person is doing it because they want to do it, not because someone orders them to do it.
examples: Helping to wash the dishes is voluntary.

senses.gloss: Working without payment.
examples: I have a voluntary position helping children learn to read.

senses.gloss: If someone releases something, they let go of it; they stop holding it and set it free (let it be free).
examples: He released his grasp on the lever.
He was released after two years in prison.

senses.gloss: Someone releases something when they put it out into the world (discharge it).
examples: They released thousands of gallons of water into the river each month.

senses.gloss: In software, a version of something that is put up for sale or that the public can use.
examples: The video store advertised that it had all the latest "releases".

senses.gloss: That which is released, untied or let go.
examples: They marked the occasion with a release of butterflies.

senses.gloss: Wealth is when one has a lot of money. Wealth is a lot of money or a lot of things of high value like land, houses, factories, jewelry, etc.
examples: His wealth is so great that he wears new shoes every day.
